title: agentHost: keep a model reference for chats that are created
body:
agentHost: keep a model reference for chats that are created

A side chat that was started with `/btw` during an active turn opened an empty widget that
never answered. `createSideChat` acquired a chat model, applied the carried-over model and
agent, then released the reference immediately. The reference count fell to zero, which
disposed the provided session and released its agent host chat subscription. The open and
send steps that followed raced that asynchronous teardown. Both steps resolved the session
content at the same time and each built an `AgentHostChatSession`. The second session
replaced the first in `_activeSessions`, but the chat model kept the first. Turn progress
went to a session that no widget observed.

- Deduplicates concurrent session resolution in `ChatSessionsService`. Callers share one
  in-flight promise. The shared work is cancelled only after every caller cancels, so one
  caller that gives up cannot abort the work of the others.
- Disposes a session that the service does not adopt. This covers the session that loses the
  cache race and a session that a provider returns after cancellation. The agent host
  provider does not honour cancellation, so it can still return a fully wired session.
- Replaces the immediate release in `createSideChat`, `forkChat`, and `_createAdditionalChat`
  with a model reference that expires after 10 seconds. The reference keeps the model alive
  across the open and send steps and cannot become permanent.
- Removes the redundant `getOrCreateChatSession` call from those three paths. The standard
  `acquireOrLoadSession` path resolves the session and owns it with a reference count.
- Logs an error when a new agent host session replaces an active session for one resource.
  This invariant was assumed in many places but was enforced in none.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332862

title: Shared prompt/customization migration attention service
body:
## Proposal

Add a shared `ICustomizationMigrationService` for editor chat and the Agents Window.

For the active workspace, the service assesses all customization types that may need migration to the Copilot harness. Third-party harness migration is out of scope.

The assessment is demand-driven and runs when:

- a new chat surface opens in the editor;
- the new-session surface opens in the Agents Window;
- an existing session is opened or restored.

It returns whether attention is needed plus categorized findings, severity, and counts. Severity distinguishes cases that remain supported or can be mapped transparently from cases that may stop working. Consumers use this result to show a consistent **customizations need attention** hint appropriate to the impact.

The assessment may also include a small sample of affected customization names if useful for the chosen UX; names are not included in telemetry.

Emit minimal telemetry from the completed assessment: trigger surface, finding category, severity, and count. Do not build separate discovery telemetry for each customization subsystem.

## Discuss

Where should the attention hint take the user to review and act on the findings?

cc @aeschli @hawkticehurst

sessions: pull request operations in the changes title bar
body:
The changes button bar in the Agents window title bar only offered "Create PR" variants, and those disappeared as soon as a pull request existed. It now keeps offering the next step for that pull request, and gives Agent Merge a home next to it.

| PR state | Primary button |
| --- | --- |
| Draft | **Mark Ready** |
| Open, mergeable | **Merge** |
| Open, not mergeable | **Enable Auto Merge** / **Disable Auto Merge** |
| Open, not mergeable, Agent Merge on | **Agent Merge** |
| Merged or closed | *(nothing)* |

The dropdown lists the other applicable pull request actions first, then a separator, then the Agent Merge entries: its session toggle, the repair-action toggles, the merge-choice submenu, and **Agent Merge Defaults** (which opens the settings editor filtered to `@tag:agentMerge`).

## Agent host

- **`AgentHostPullRequestStatusService`** (new) watches the `core` and `mergeability` fragments of the session's pull request. It subscribes only while a client is subscribed to the session's changeset, so the GitHub API cost is bounded to the session the user is actually looking at.
- **`AgentHostPullRequestOperationContribution`** advertises `pr-mark-ready`, `pr-merge` and `pr-enable-auto-merge` / `pr-disable-auto-merge` instead of bailing out once a pull request exists. Auto-merge is driven off GitHub's own capability flags (`viewerCanEnableAutoMerge` is already false for a PR that can simply be merged) rather than re-deriving its rules here. Nothing is advertised while the state is unresolved — the bar stays hidden rather than flashing the wrong action — or once the PR is merged or closed.
- **`AgentHostPullRequestLifecycleOperationHandler`** (new) executes them. Merging goes through `prepareMerge`, so a pull request that stopped being mergeable between the button being rendered and clicked is rejected rather than force-merged, and enqueues when the repository requires a merge queue.
- Adds the `markReadyForReview` and `disableAutoMerge` GitHub mutations, which the mutation service was missing.

## Agents window

- New `MenuId.AgentsChangesOperationsDropdown`, whose entries are merged into the primary button's dropdown. A submenu contributed to its `primary` group *names* a group of related actions rather than being one, so clicking the button opens exactly those as a context menu — the arrow dropdown also carries unrelated pull request operations, so it would be wrong to run its first entry.
- Agent Merge registers its entries there, gated on the existing `chat.agentMerge.enabled` precondition plus the session having an open pull request.

## `chat.agentMerge.mergePullRequest` becomes a three-way enum

`always` | `ifUnchanged` | `never`, defaulting to `never`. Existing boolean values migrate (`true` → `always`, `false` → `never`) in the settings migration, the legacy-key migration, and when reading session overrides from disk.

`ifUnchanged` merges only while Agent Merge has not changed the pull request. It is self-demoting rather than evaluated at merge time: the head SHA is recorded when a repair turn starts, and if a later head differs that turn landed a commit, so the session's value rewrites itself to `never` and posts a notice in the transcript. That way the chosen value always reflects what will actually happen, and the submenu title shows it — `Merge Pull Request (Never)` — without having to open it. Re-selecting `ifUnchanged` clears the baseline and starts fresh.

A repair turn that pushed nothing (for example one that only replied to a review comment) leaves auto-merge on.

## Logging

Because "why is *this* button showing" spans four layers, each one logs its transitions (deduped against a signature, so steady state is silent):

- `AgentHostPullRequestStatusService` logs every flag the button choice branches on, and names the reason when a session is *not* being watched (archived, no subscriber, no PR for the branch, account/host mismatch).
- The operation provider logs the advertised set, calling out the primary separately.
- The lifecycle handler logs invocation, the merge-queue decision, and failures.
- The widget logs the rendered button with a `source` of `running-operation`, `contributed-menu` or `advertised-operation`.

## Validation

Clean `typecheck-client` and `valid-layers-check`. 50 node tests and 31 browser tests pass across the touched areas, including new coverage for the operation state machine, the two new mutations, the boolean→enum migration, and the six demotion cases.

## Note for reviewers

**Merge has no confirmation dialog** — one click merges, by design. The `prepareMerge` gate is what makes that safe.

The demotion notice reuses `AgentSystemNotificationKind.AgentMergeDisabled`, so it renders like the existing auto-disable notice. If it should be visually distinct from "Agent Merge turned itself off entirely", that needs a new notification kind.

title: Re-enable Chat Sandbox smoke tests in Remote runs
body:
## Summary

Chat Sandbox smoke tests have been temporarily disabled for Remote smoke-test runs in PR #332892.

The suite itself was previously registered for every non-web run, including Remote. However, the `vscode-smoketest-ext-host` helper extension is copied into the smoke-test extensions directory only for non-web, non-Remote runs. That extension contributes `smoketest.openLocalChat`, which the Chat Sandbox suite invokes in its `before` hook to open the built-in Local test harness.

As a result, `smoketest.openLocalChat` is not present in the Command Palette during Remote runs.

## Why this appeared to work before

Before PR #332892, `QuickAccess.runCommand()` typed the requested command ID into the Command Palette but accepted any focused result unless the row said `No matching commands`. When `smoketest.openLocalChat` was absent, the Command Palette returned another fuzzy chat-related result and automation accepted it. This masked the missing helper command.

PR #332892 makes command automation verify the selected item's exact command ID by default. Linux and macOS Remote smoke tests then failed deterministically with:

```
Error: QuickAccess.runCommand(command: smoketest.openLocalChat, match: exactCommandId) failed to find command.
```

Returning this call to fuzzy matching would hide the setup problem and could execute an unrelated command, so the suite is temporarily gated with `!opts.remote` instead.

## How Remote coverage could be re-enabled

Possible approaches:

1. Make `vscode-smoketest-ext-host` available in Remote smoke runs. It declares `extensionKind: ["ui"]`, so the setup should ensure it is installed in the correct local/UI extension location and that `smoketest.openLocalChat` is registered before the suite invokes it.
2. Replace the helper with exact UI-visible commands and interactions that select the Local test harness. The underlying `workbench.action.chat.newLocalChat` command currently has `f1: false`, which is why the helper command exists.
3. If Chat Sandbox is intentionally unsupported in Remote configurations, keep the exclusion and document that limitation explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria

- Re-enable `setupChatSandboxTests(logger)` for Remote smoke runs.
- Ensure the requested command or replacement UI flow exists in Remote and is selected using exact matching.
- Verify the Chat Sandbox suite passes in Linux and macOS Remote smoke jobs without relying on an unrelated fuzzy Command Palette result.

Related: #332892

title: agentHost: Prefer stored Copilot restore metadata
body:
Fixes #332885

## What changed

- Pass stable registry timestamps to provider metadata reads during explicit session restore.
- Restore registered Copilot sessions from VS Code-persisted working-directory and project metadata when available.
- Skip the redundant SDK metadata lookup before resume when VS Code already has the working directory.
- Preserve SDK metadata lookups for external and legacy sessions.

## Why

A Copilot SDK `session.getMetadata` request can remain pending for an affected persisted session, preventing Agent Host state hydration. Registered Agent Host sessions already retain the metadata needed to begin restore, so the restore path can avoid depending on that request when the stored metadata is complete.

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Targeted Agent Host tests for restore activation, SDK lookup preservation, stored metadata restore, and resume fallback

title: Support GitHub Copilot authentication in Azure DevOps pipelines for automated VS Code chat participant testing
body:
## Scenario

We want to run automated end-to-end tests for a VS Code chat participant from an Azure DevOps (ADO) CI pipeline.

The chat participant uses the VS Code Language Model API (`vscode.lm`) and requires GitHub Copilot authentication and service access. The pipeline must launch VS Code, invoke the chat participant, and validate its behavior without interactive user input.

## Problem

GitHub Copilot authentication is normally associated with an interactive, licensed GitHub user. An ADO service connection, workload identity, or service principal does not appear to provide GitHub Copilot entitlement.

We want to avoid unsupported approaches such as:

- Using a developer's personal credentials
- Exporting or copying VS Code credential storage
- Automating OAuth or device-login prompts
- Injecting undocumented access tokens

## Questions

1. What is the supported way to authenticate GitHub Copilot from an ADO CI pipeline?
2. Can an ADO workload identity, service principal, GitHub App, or other machine identity receive Copilot access?
3. Is a dedicated GitHub automation account with a Copilot Business/Enterprise seat supported for automated testing?
4. Can a persistent self-hosted ADO agent authenticate once and securely reuse its VS Code/Copilot session?
5. Is there a supported credential provider, environment variable, or CI test identity for GitHub Copilot?
6. What is the recommended approach for automated E2E testing of VS Code chat participants that depend on `vscode.lm`?

## Intended environment

- Azure DevOps CI pipeline
- Windows agent, self-hosted if required
- VS Code launched through UI automation
- A VS Code extension contributing a chat participant
- GitHub Copilot as the language-model provider
- No interactive authentication during pipeline execution

We are looking for an officially supported and secure solution for granting the pipeline GitHub Copilot authentication and access.

title: Chat: unify Agent Host status pills across chat surfaces
body:
## Summary

This pull request brings Agent Host session status pills to editor and panel chat inputs and, more importantly, consolidates the Agents Window and editor/panel implementations onto the same reusable pill architecture.

The result is one shared composition and lifecycle path for Changes, Pull Requests, Issues, Artifacts, References, Browsers, Customizations, and Subagents. Each surface now supplies observable data and an allowed set of pill kinds; it no longer independently decides ordering, rendering, compact behavior, visibility, keyboard behavior, or dropdown mechanics.

## User experience

- Shows session status pills above the chat input for Agent Host-backed editor and panel chats.
- Keeps Local chat inputs pill-free. The editor/panel integration is intentionally Agent Host-specific.
- Offers these editor/panel pill kinds:
  - Changes
  - Pull Requests
  - Issues
  - Artifacts
  - References
  - Browsers
- Keeps Agents Window-only data such as Customizations and Subagents available in the Agents Window without exposing inappropriate worktree-specific UI in editor/panel chat.
- Uses the existing `chat.turnStatusPills` setting, which remains enabled by default.
- Preserves chat pet interaction by publishing the same rendered pill elements as horizontal pet platforms.
- Uses responsive compact behavior in smaller chat surfaces: pills remain expanded while they fit and collapse to icon-only presentation only when the row would overflow.

## Shared architecture

### One controller for both surfaces

`ChatInputPills` now owns the common row and widget lifecycle:

- setting enablement;
- per-kind user visibility;
- the visibility context menu and hidden-pill recovery state;
- row and widget creation;
- keyboard and focus restoration;
- chat pet element publication;
- visible/hidden lifecycle notifications.

Both the Agents Window and Agent Host editor/panel adapter instantiate this controller instead of maintaining separate toolbar implementations.

### One canonical pill composition

`StandardChatInputPillSources` is the canonical builder for the standard session pill set. It owns:

- pill ordering;
- component selection;
- Changes rendering and activation;
- Pull Request, Issue, Artifact, Reference, Browser, Customization, and Subagent section pills;
- shared per-kind labels, icons, summaries, and single-entry behavior.

The two surfaces only provide observable sections, callbacks, and the kinds they support. This prevents presentation drift such as the previously different Pull Request pill between the Agents Window and editor chat.

### Shared presentation helpers

- Common Pull Request state-to-icon and aggregate-priority logic moved into shared workbench code.
- Common session pill options moved into a shared options module.
- Live Pull Request presentation is resolved once through a reusable Sessions model, while polling remains centrally owned by the existing GitHub polling contribution.
- Provider-specific session and changeset resolution remains in Agent Host connection/provider policy rather than being reconstructed by the UI.

### Removed duplicate pill path

The old `SessionHeaderMeta` metadata-pill path is no longer needed after the input toolbar migration. This change removes:

- `SessionMetadataPills`;
- specialized Changes, Pull Request, and Issue header action view items;
- their action-view-item registrations;
- legacy component fixtures and tests that exercised the now-unreachable header implementation.

The commands themselves remain available for the shared pills and session context menus. This leaves a single active rendering architecture instead of two independently evolving implementations.

## Flicker and lifecycle improvements

The shared pill primitives were updated to avoid rebuilding UI for routine observable changes:

- Pill membership updates are incremental and preserve existing DOM nodes.
- Existing pill buttons and keyboard focus survive unrelated pill additions and removals.
- An open dropdown remains open when an unrelated pill changes.
- If the open pill itself disappears, focus moves to the nearest remaining pill, the empty configuration row, or the owning chat input.
- Open dropdown contents update in place when their observable sections change and close when the pill is no longer summarized.
- Stable section-pill descriptors prevent toolbar recreation while visible presentation is unchanged.
- Dropdown buttons update only the label, tooltip, icon, and accessibility state that actually changed.
- Responsive compact measurement caches intrinsic pill width instead of repeatedly measuring the viewport-sized row.
- The intrinsic-width cache is invalidated only when pill sizing changes.
- Agent Host change summaries retain the last authoritative files during transient changeset recomputation and clear only when a ready changeset is authoritatively empty.
- Change caches are isolated by connection authority and changeset URI.

These changes address the visible flashing during session startup, new pill discovery, changeset recomputation, and session completion.

## Agent Host and GitHub correctness

- Editor/panel pills resolve the backend session URI, scheme aliases, relative changeset templates, and configured default changeset kind through shared Agent Host connection policy.
- Cloud Sandbox aliases therefore resolve to the correct backend session and changeset channel.
- Browser pills include browsers owned by direct tool-origin subagent chats.
- Hiding the Browser pill allows matching website artifacts or references to appear in their corresponding pills instead of disappearing entirely.
- Pull Request state is applied only to the URL it describes; unrelated Pull Requests keep their own open/default state.
- Pull Request summary icons are derived from the per-entry icons using shared priority rules.
- Agents Window Pull Request pills retain live CI/review state and Agent Merge-aware blocker presentation.
- Combined failing-check and unresolved-review states are announced together.
- Cached draft, merged, and closed Pull Request icons retain matching accessible state before live details arrive.
- Pull Request polling is not duplicated by the presentation layer.
- Issue refresh/polling only runs while the Issue pill feature is enabled and visible.

## Accessibility

- The row and pills keep consistent toolbar, button, listbox, and popup semantics.
- The empty hidden-pill recovery row is keyboard accessible and exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"`.
- Inline single-entry and single-resource pills expose both their actionable label and their status/location description.
- Focus is preserved across incremental updates and safely restored when a focused or expanded pill disappears.
- Auxiliary-window rendering uses the correct DOM realm and target-window observers.
- Sessions accessibility help now describes status pills above the chat input rather than the removed session-header controls.

## Validation

Validated after rebasing onto the latest `main`:

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint across all TypeScript files changed by the PR
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- 197 focused workbench, Sessions, Agent Host changeset, GitHub, accessibility, and pill unit tests
- forced `npm run build-fast -- --force`
- Component Explorer checks for:
  - the shared `3 Pull Requests` summary/dropdown presentation;
  - the `1 File +12 -5` Changes presentation;
  - responsive expanded/compact behavior.

title: Fix chat notifications to be session scoped
body:
This pull request addresses issues with chat notifications by implementing session-scoped behavior. The changes include:

- Refactoring the notification architecture to allow for per-input content and actions, improving the user experience when switching models.
- Introducing a new `resolveBody(context)` callback to simplify how notification content is determined based on the input's context.
- Restoring existing action fallbacks and ensuring that notifications are correctly announced by screen readers.
- Fixing lifecycle issues related to panel auto-dismiss and quota warnings, ensuring that notifications behave correctly across different input states.

The overall size of the changes has been optimized, with a net reduction in lines of code while maintaining comprehensive test coverage. This update aims to enhance the functionality and reliability of chat notifications in the application.

title: agentHost: avoid SDK metadata lookup during session restore
body:
Prevents registered Agent Host Copilot sessions from blocking before SDK resume when `getSessionMetadata` does not settle. Once the Copilot SDK/runtime bump is reintroduced, existing sessions with complete host-owned persistence can hydrate and proceed directly to `resumeSession`.

Provider-native sessions and incomplete legacy sessions still use the SDK metadata lookup because VS Code does not have sufficient local state for them.

Fixes #332885

## How

- Pass stable registry timestamps into activating provider metadata reads.
- Build registered Copilot restore metadata from the persisted title, project, and working directories.
- Avoid the second SDK metadata lookup before resume when a persisted working directory is available.
- Cover fallback propagation, metadata hydration without an SDK request, and cold resume without an SDK metadata request.

## Current status

The SDK/runtime bump was reverted from `main` in #332951, so the failure is no longer reproducible on current `main`; this draft preserves the proposed hardening for the next adoption attempt.

A clean OSS build at the exact first-bad commit `a29f231dfa3` (`@github/copilot-sdk` `1.0.13-preview.0`, runtime `1.0.81-12`) did not reproduce the issue. The persisted `Sanity test Copilot SDK` session reached SDK resume and restored 25 turns in about 2.6 seconds. Per the requested validation rule, no with-fix OSS comparison was run, so this proposal remains unvalidated against a reproducing baseline.

The exact-bad product and all built-in extensions compiled with zero errors before the attempt. The source diff passes `git diff --check`.

title: Files opened read-only by "ReadOnly Include" cannot be made writable via "Reset Active Editor Read-Only In Session"
body: Type: Bug If a file has been opened in read-only mode via `ReadOnly Include`, an attempt to unlock it for changes via `Reset Active Editor Read-Only In Session` fails. Use Case: I do a lot of review and don't want to make inadvertent changes to the files I am reviewing, so I would like to open them _by default_ as read-only. But in the cases where I _do_ decide I want to make changes, I should be able to do so by explicitly unlocking that file interactively while it's open in the editor using the existing mechanism for doing that. 1. Add a file path to `ReadOnly Include` using `/.../**` glob format 2. Open a file under that path 3. File opens as locked Read Only - good 4. Attempt to execute `Reset Active Editor Read-Only In Session` in that tab 5. Editor tab remains locked in read-only, edits rejected - bad If the user defined paths via `Readonly Include`, the user should have the option to override that _interactively_ on a _case-by-case basis_. If `Reset Active Editor Read-Only In Session` should _not_ be allowed to globally override files locked by `Readonly Include`, then it would be acceptable to gate this capability either globally (e.g. `[_] Allow Override Of Readonly Include In Editor`) or via a similar list of file paths (i.e. divide `Readonly Include` into `Readonly Include Initial` + `Readonly Include Hard`, or a new `Allow Readonly Unlock In Editor` filepath list to mark which `Readonly Include` folders are by-default vs. hard) This of course does not apply to files that are read-only due to filesystem permissions that the user cannot override. body:
## Feature request

Add `gpt-5.4-nano` as an explicit option for the experimental dictation LLM cleanup backend model.

Today, `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` supports `auto`, `copilot-utility-small`, and `gpt-5.6-luna`. GPT-5.4 Nano is a small, low-latency model that is well suited to punctuation, capitalization, paragraph, list, and numeric-format cleanup.

## Proposed behavior

- Add `gpt-5.4-nano` to the `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` setting.
- Resolve it through a core-only Copilot language-model alias so hidden backend models remain unavailable to extensions and the model picker.
- Fall back to `copilot-utility-small` when GPT-5.4 Nano is unavailable, preserving the raw-transcript fallback if no cleanup model is available.
- Track the selected backend in existing dictation cleanup telemetry.

## Acceptance criteria

- Selecting `gpt-5.4-nano` routes cleanup requests to the GPT-5.4 Nano backend.
- The alias is only callable by VS Code core and is not user-selectable in the general model picker.
- Existing `auto`, utility-small, and Luna behavior remains unchanged.
- Unit tests cover selection, fallback, and alias visibility/access.

title: Show an "External Session" row in the sessions list hover
body:
The sessions list hover in the Agents window gave no indication that a session was picked up from another application, and no way to reach the setting that governs whether those sessions appear at all. This adds a trailing, separated **External Session** row that links to that setting.

The row shows only when `ISession.isExternal` is set, and behaves like the other hover links — activating it opens the settings editor revealing `chat.agentSessions.showExternal`.

### Changes

- **`sessionSummaryHover.ts`** — new optional `externalSession` field on `ISessionSummaryHoverData`, rendered as a final `.session-summary-hover-section`. Sections already carry a `border-top`, so the separator comes for free; reusing `_appendButtonRow` gives the row the same link styling, hover color and focus outline as `Created by`.
- **`sessionHoverContent.ts`** — the Agents-window adapter populates the field from `session.isExternal`, opening the setting via `IPreferencesService.openSettings({ jsonEditor: false, query: '@id:chat.agentSessions.showExternal' })`, matching how other chat surfaces reveal a single setting.
- **`sessionsList.ts` / `openSessionLinkOpener.contribution.ts`** — thread `IPreferencesService` through the row renderer and the session-pill hover provider, which share the adapter.
- **Tests / fixture** — coverage that an external session's row targets the right setting query and a local session has none, plus a `SessionHover_ExternalSession` component fixture.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Fix authentication redirect loop · Claude │
│ Workspace · ~/projects/vscode            │
│ Branch · main                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ⧉ External Session                       │  ← clickable, opens Settings
└────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Notes for review

- The setting is read through the existing `ChatConfiguration.ShowExternalAgentSessions` constant rather than a literal, so the `@id:` query stays in sync.
- `isExternal` is read when the hover content is built; `setupDelayedHover` re-invokes the factory on each hover, so this matches the other non-reactive fields (`title`, `changes`).
- The row is intentionally added in the shared adapter, so the `agent-host-session://` pill hover in chat output picks it up too.

title: Add "Continue with Microsoft" sign in for GitHub
body:
Lets someone already signed in to Microsoft reach Copilot without a second trip through the browser. The `microsoft` provider already holds an Entra token; this trades it for a GitHub one.

## How the flow works

Two exchanges, on purpose.

The first buys a `read:user` discovery token, just enough to call `GET /user` and find out which GitHub account the Entra identity maps to. That account is shown to the user, and nothing is published until they confirm it. The second exchange then mints the scopes the caller actually asked for.

The discovery token is never persisted and never published as a session. Neither token is ever logged.

## What survives a reload

Entra-brokered sessions live in memory for the life of the window and never touch the Keychain. What persists is the user's consent: a row in global state holding the GitHub account label, the Microsoft account label, and the GitHub user id. A fresh window mints the session again from that row without prompting, re-running discovery to confirm the row still points at the same account.

Rows are keyed by GitHub account label, because that is what VS Code itself keys an account by. `getAccounts` collapses sessions by label and the account preference is stored by label. A session read back from the Keychain can carry a placeholder id, an old numeric one, or one from a lookup that failed, so the id is no way to tell two accounts apart. The id has exactly one job here: checking that the token GitHub just returned belongs to the account the row names, which a label cannot do because logins get renamed and freed logins get taken.

## Signing out

Signing out of GitHub drops the row. Signing out of Microsoft drops the sessions, since nothing can renew them, but deliberately leaves the rows alone.

That asymmetry matters. The Microsoft account list is a per-window cache that legitimately reads empty for a moment while it repopulates, and the rows are global state shared by every window. Acting on a blink of that list would sign the user out everywhere with no way back. Dropping only the in-memory sessions self-heals: the next read mints them again from the row that is still there. Getting it wrong costs one round trip instead of the account.

## Testing

37 unit tests pass across `accountLinks.test.ts`, `entraTokenExchange.test.ts`, `flows.test.ts`, plus the workbench tests in `chatSetup.test.ts` and `defaultAccount.test.ts`. End to end this was exercised through sign in, window reload, cross-window sign in from the Agents window, and both sign-out paths.

## Note for reviewers

`extensions/github-authentication/src/config.ts` is intentionally untouched here. The client secret this endpoint requires lives in vscode-distro, not in this repo.

Draft while the endpoint registration is finalized.

title: Keep the full URI reachable in the prompt URL confirmation dialog
body:
The confirmation dialog shown when installing a prompt / instructions / agent file from a URL truncates the URI in the middle: ```ts uriLabel = `${uriLabel.substring(0, 35)}...${uriLabel.substring(uriLabel.length - 15)}`; ``` Because the middle is what gets removed, the host can end up entirely inside the hidden part. For example ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com.cdn.example.com/copilot-instructions.md ``` renders in the dialog as ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com.c...instructions.md ``` which reads as a `raw.githubusercontent.com` URL, while the request actually goes elsewhere. `extensionUrlHandler` truncates the same way, but keeps the full URI reachable. That was added in #239527 ("Provide a way to reveal the entire URI in an 'Allow extension to open URI' dialog", fixes #239272): ```ts new MarkdownString(`
${uriLabel}
`, { supportHtml: true }) ``` The prompt dialog renders its label as a markdown link, so it does get `title` automatically from the renderer (`markdownRenderer.ts`: `effectiveTitle = title || href`), but it has no `aria-label`. The accessible name of the link is therefore the truncated text, and a screen reader user has no way to reach the real host. This change emits the link as HTML and sets both `title` and `aria-label` to the full URI, matching what `extensionUrlHandler` already does. Two things I checked before proposing this: - `URI.toString()` percent-encodes `"`, `'`, `<` and `>`, so interpolating it into the attributes cannot break out of them. - Anchors coming from raw HTML are handled exactly like markdown links: `markdownRenderer.ts` walks every `a[href]` in the rendered root and moves the href to `data-href`, and the click/keydown listeners are attached to the container. Click behaviour is unchanged.

title: Copilot Chat agent todo list never completes after the task is finished
body:
## Description
When using Copilot Chat in agent mode with a plan, Copilot creates a todo
list ("Todos (1/4)", etc.). Even after the agent completes the entire request
(files edited, final summary shown), the todo list is never fully checked off.
Items are left in an in-progress state with a spinner indefinitely, so there is
no way to know whether the agent truly finished all the work.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Ask Copilot Chat to perform a multi-step task in agent/plan mode so it
   creates a todo list.
2. Let it run to completion: it edits files and posts its final summary
   (e.g. "Created 4 todos", "Reviewed and updated offer-detail.php").
3. Look at the todo list panel: it stays at e.g. "Todos (1/4)" with the
   remaining items still shown as in-progress/spinner, never checked off.

## Expected Behavior
When the agent finishes the request, all todo items should be marked
completed so the user can trust the work is done.

## Actual Behavior
The todo list remains stuck mid-progress (e.g. 1/4), items left with an active
status/spinner, even after the agent has finished all steps and posted its
summary. The user cannot tell whether the task succeeded.

## Additional Information
- Affected models: ChatGPT 5.6 Luna (my main Copilot model, the most used —
  it fails consistently) and Gemini 3.7 Flash (I switched to it for this request
  to check whether the bug also happens with another Copilot model — it does).
- I have never seen this problem when using models brought in via BYOK
  (e.g. an external provider like Opencode Go). This suggests the issue is
  specific to GitHub's own Copilot models rather than the todo list UI itself.

## Impact
Every agent session creates uncertainty about completion. Workarounds
(asking the agent "are you done? update your todos") waste context and
server resources.

title: sessions: fix broken "Sent from another chat" request-origin link
body:
## What

Fixes two independent bugs that broke the "Sent from another chat" / "Sent by another session" request-origin link (the small pill shown above a delegated chat request, linking back to the chat/session that sent it).

## Why

1. **Agents window** — `OpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution` fell back to a bare `openSession()` when the link carried no chat id. Per `buildOpenSessionLinkUri`'s documented invariant, an absent chat id means "the session's default chat," but `openSession()` only activates the session without switching the active chat. So clicking the pill was a no-op whenever a *different* chat of the same session (e.g. a peer/subagent chat) was already showing — exactly the case when a delegated request originates from the session's default chat.
2. **Regular editor window** — `AgentHostOpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution` only registered an opener with `IOpenerService` (for markdown-authored links), never with `IChatRequestOriginService` (which is what the pill's click handler actually calls). So clicking the pill found no opener and fell back to treating the opaque `agent-host-session://` link as a session resource directly, which never resolves.

## Fix

- `OpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution._open()` now always resolves a concrete target chat — the peer chat when a chat id is present, otherwise the session's `mainChat` — and opens it uniformly via `ISessionsService.openChat()`.
- `AgentHostOpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution` now also registers a request-origin opener that reuses its existing link-opening logic.

## Testing

- Added a regression test for each fix, reproducing the exact metadata shape captured from a live repro (delegation link with no chat id, and a request-origin link opened from the editor window).
- Updated an existing test that encoded the old (buggy) "no chat id → openSession" expectation.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and `npm run hygiene` all pass clean.

title: VSCode Agents should not be a marketing tool for Copilot
body:
I wish to complain about Microsoft’s decision to restrict or gate VS Code’s integrated agent functionality behind a GitHub Copilot subscription when the agent being used is supplied and paid for independently.

I use Visual Studio Code as my development environment and already subscribe to, and use, third-party coding agents including OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code. I have no requirement for GitHub Copilot and do not wish to purchase a Copilot Pro subscription.

VS Code is increasingly presenting an integrated “Agents” experience which appears, from a user’s perspective, to be a general-purpose framework for running coding agents. However, access to parts of that interface and functionality has been tied to GitHub Copilot subscriptions, even where the underlying agent is not Copilot and where the user already has a direct subscription to the third-party provider.

I consider this an unreasonable product restriction.

There is a legitimate distinction between charging for Microsoft's own AI service and charging for VS Code functionality. If I ask Microsoft to provide inference, models, compute capacity or other Copilot services, then requiring a Copilot subscription is entirely understandable.

That is not what I am asking for.

I want VS Code to act as the development environment and user interface for agents for which I already have separate access and subscriptions. In that situation, Microsoft is providing the editor integration, not the AI service itself.

Requiring me to buy GitHub Copilot Pro merely to make full use of VS Code's agent interface with Codex or Claude Code amounts, in practical terms, to bundling Microsoft's paid AI product with access to editor functionality that should be independent of the choice of AI provider.

This is particularly disappointing given VS Code's history as an open and extensible development environment. Developers have traditionally been able to choose their compilers, source-control providers, language servers, debuggers, extensions and other development tools independently. AI coding agents should follow the same model.

I would therefore ask Microsoft to adopt a clear separation between:

1. **VS Code agent-host functionality**, which should be available to VS Code users independently of a Copilot subscription; and
2. **GitHub Copilot services**, for which a Copilot subscription can reasonably be required.

Users should be able to authenticate directly with OpenAI, Anthropic and other supported agent providers and use those agents through the VS Code agent interface without purchasing a redundant GitHub Copilot subscription.

I appreciate that Microsoft appears to be moving partially in this direction with newer Agent Host functionality and provider-native authentication. However, the current experience remains confusing and unnecessarily restricted, with some capabilities and documentation still treating Copilot as a prerequisite.

I would therefore like Microsoft to:

* remove any Copilot subscription requirement for VS Code agent functionality where Microsoft is not supplying the underlying AI service;
* allow direct provider authentication throughout the VS Code Agents experience;
* ensure custom VS Code agents can invoke supported third-party agent harnesses without requiring Copilot;
* clearly distinguish in the UI between functionality supplied by VS Code and services supplied by GitHub Copilot; and
* avoid designing future VS Code agent functionality in a way that makes Copilot a compulsory intermediary for competing AI services.

I am not requesting free access to GitHub Copilot. Quite the opposite: I do not want to use GitHub Copilot.

I simply want to be able to use the AI services I have independently chosen and paid for within my chosen development environment, without being required to purchase Microsoft's competing AI service as an additional prerequisite.

I would appreciate this complaint being passed to the VS Code product team responsible for the Agents architecture and commercial integration with GitHub Copilot, and I would welcome a substantive response explaining Microsoft's intended policy for third-party, independently authenticated coding agents in VS Code.

title: agentHost: don't tell the agent to reply-and-stop after create_session
body:
Fixes #330138

### Problem
After a request like "spawn a session for X and then do Y", creating the child session caused the parent to stop early instead of continuing with Y.

The `create_session` / `send_message` server tools instructed the model to **"Reply with one short sentence confirming the … was created"** — in both the tool *result* and the tool *description*. The model read that as a turn terminator, so it created the session and stopped.

### Change
- **Results** are now neutral statements of fact, carrying the open link with no reply-and-stop imperative:
  - `New session created (agent-host-session://…).`
  - `Chat created in the current session (…).`
  - `Chat created (…).`
  - `Message sent (…).`
- **Descriptions** are now purely functional: dropped the UI-presentation policy ("the UI renders…", "don't print the URL", "don't tell the user to click a button") and the "reply with a single short sentence" instruction. Presentation is the client's concern; the result already carries the link.
- Added a focused regression test locking both the neutral results and the functional descriptions.
- Regenerated the 19 Copilot prompt snapshots for the updated descriptions (tokenless replay update).

This preserves the #332225 rollback intent — no child-session orchestration/fan-in code is touched.

### Validation
- Targeted node unit suite (`sessionServerTools.test.ts`) — 56 passing incl. the new regression test.
- Prompt-snapshot suite regenerated and green (22 passing); e2e replay captures unaffected (tool_result payloads are elided from the request projection).
- `typecheck-client` clean; eslint clean on changed files.

### Reviewer note / known limitation
Removing the explicit stop signal is a real improvement, but it is a **mitigation, not a guarantee**. The agent host runs a model-driven loop, so after *any* tool result the model itself decides whether to continue or end the turn — a debug-log capture on a patched build still showed the parent occasionally ending with an empty terminal message after `create_session`. A fully reliable fix would be structural (e.g. an `onTurnEnd` continuation nudge for the side-effect-tool class, with a loop guard). Discussion and a question for @roblourens are on #330138.

title: agentHost: Stop customization refresh after session removal
body:
I generated this by scanning my logs, pls take if it's good/useful

---

🤖

## Summary

Prevents an asynchronous Agent Host customization refresh from publishing into a session that was removed while customization discovery was still pending.

## Symptom

Recent Code - Insiders Agent Host logs contained warnings such as:

```text
2026-08-25 16:02:20.956 [info] [Copilot] Chat created; its backing stays deferred until the first send: copilotcli:/9d927329-1762-430f-a91b-a10ca927afcf
2026-08-25 16:02:23.072 [warning] [AgentHostStateManager] Action for unknown session: copilotcli:/9d927329-1762-430f-a91b-a10ca927afcf, type=session/customizationsChanged
```

The warning means a provider-side customization refresh produced a state action after the target session had already left the state manager.

## Root cause

`AgentSideEffects._publishSessionCustomizations` reads the session's current customizations, awaits `agent.getChatCustomizations(...)`, and then compares the newly resolved set against the current session state before dispatching `session/customizationsChanged`.

Previously, both reads used optional chaining directly on `getSessionState(...)`. This collapsed two distinct states to the same value:

- an existing session whose customizations have not been published yet; and
- a session that was removed while discovery was pending.

Both yielded `undefined`. Consequently, if the session disappeared during the `await`, the existing deduplication/supersession logic could still reach `dispatchServerAction` and emit an action for an unknown session.

## Fix

- Require the session to exist before starting customization discovery.
- Recheck that it still exists after the asynchronous discovery completes.
- Preserve the existing structural deduplication and superseded-refresh retry behavior for live sessions.

The guard is intentionally at the asynchronous producer rather than in `AgentHostStateManager`: unknown-session warnings remain useful for finding other stale producers, while this refresh simply has no valid target after removal.

## Test coverage

Adds a regression test that:

1. starts customization discovery;
2. waits until discovery is pending;
3. removes the session from the state manager;
4. completes discovery; and
5. verifies that no `SessionCustomizationsChanged` envelope is emitted.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSideEffects.test.ts --grep "customizations"` - 9 passing
- pre-commit hygiene - passed for both changed files
- `git diff --check`

## Reviewer note

The main point to verify is that the explicit existence checks preserve the intended idle-eviction/restore behavior: a later refresh for a restored session with the same URI still publishes normally, while an in-flight refresh belonging to the removed incarnation is dropped.

title: BYOK OpenRouter: hover shows Max context 1M instead of 256K for ":free" variants (discovery prefers top-level context_length over top_provider.context_length)
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: GitHub.copilot-chat 0.63.0 (bundled with 1.135.0); 0.62.0 (1.134.0) when first reported
- VS Code Version: 1.135.0 — still reproduces; original report from 1.134.0
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations (10.0.26200), 64-bit
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Chat model picker — BYOK (Manage Language Models) / OpenRouter provider
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Poolside: Laguna S 2.1 (free) via OpenRouter BYOK group (`vendor: "openrouter"`)
- Logs: Discovery works without errors, nothing relevant in Output → "GitHub Copilot Chat". The root cause is reproducible with two public unauthenticated HTTP calls (see Root cause). Can attach `Developer: GitHub Copilot Chat Diagnostics` output on request.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Model picker → ⚙️ Manage Language Models → Add Models → OpenRouter → enter API key, create a group.
2. Hover the model "Poolside: Laguna S 2.1 (free)" in the picker.
   The hover card shows: **Max context 1M**.
3. Compare with https://openrouter.ai/poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free — the documented limit for this route is **256K** (262144 tokens).
   Note: the paid sibling `poolside/laguna-s-2.1` shows its correct 1M, so the bug only affects variants whose real cap differs from the parent model.

## Root cause

The built-in OpenRouter provider discovers models via:

    GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models?supported_parameters=tools

and resolves capabilities approximately as (from the bundled minified provider):

```js
const a = entry.context_length ?? entry.top_provider.context_length; // ← prefers top-level
const c = Math.min(entry.top_provider.max_completion_tokens ?? 16000, Math.floor(a / 2));
// maxInputTokens = a - c, maxOutputTokens = c
// hover "Max context" = maxInputTokens + maxOutputTokens = a
```

On this filtered endpoint OpenRouter reports the parent paid model's `context_length`
at top level, while the true free-route cap is only present under `top_provider`.
Since the top-level field wins via `??`, VS Code surfaces the parent's limit.

Measured 2026-08-27, stable across repeated calls, no auth required:

```text
$ curl -s 'https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models?supported_parameters=tools' \
    | jq '.data[] | select(.id=="poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free") | {context_length, top_provider}'
{
  "context_length": 1048576,                                          ← parent value (wrong for :free)
  "top_provider": { "context_length": 262144, "max_completion_tokens": 32768 }
}

$ curl -s 'https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models' \
    | jq '.data[] | select(.id=="poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free") | .context_length'
262144                                                                 ← consistent
```

So `a = 1048576`, `c = 32768`, total = 1048576 → picker advertises "1M".

Upstream: the same catalog inconsistency has been reported to OpenRouter (official Discord, `#feedback-and-requests`, 2026-08-27): https://discord.com/channels/1091220969173028894/1542502332435267604 — link resolves for OpenRouter Discord members only; the post contains the same repro and links back to this issue.


## Impact

The context-usage indicator and prompt truncation are computed from
`maxInputTokens + maxOutputTokens`. Requests above 262,144 tokens fail against
this free route even though the picker advertises 1M.

## Suggested fix

Prefer the smallest known limit instead of relying on field order:

```js
const ctx = Math.min(
    entry.context_length ?? Infinity,
    entry.top_provider?.context_length ?? entry.context_length
);
```

This stays correct for all current vendor response shapes (OpenRouter, Anthropic, xAI).

## Workaround

Re-declare the affected models through the Custom Endpoint provider with explicit
`maxInputTokens` / `maxOutputTokens` (e.g. 229376 / 32768 for this model) — then the
picker shows the correct window regardless of catalog data.

title: sessions: refine the session hover in the sessions list
body:
Reworks how a session's hover reads in the Agents window sessions list, so the things that identify a session land first and the supporting detail stays quiet behind them. ### What changed - **The agent moves onto the title line** — `Fix the redirect loop · Claude` — replacing the muted `Copilot · Local Agent Host` footer that used to close the hover. Which provider serves the session was never the point; the kind of agent is part of its identity, so it belongs beside the title. - **One color for the location block.** Workspace path, worktree path and branch now share the muted color the worktree path already had, so the block reads as a single unit instead of three competing weights. - **A worktree is carried by its icon alone.** Naming it "Worktree" next to the path only crowded the row. - **Pending changes get their own row**, below the branch and led by the multi-diff icon, instead of trailing the branch behind a separator. - **Pull request rows became links.** They take the link color on hover and open the pull request when pressed (the state icon keeps its own color, so a merged PR still reads as merged). - **Home paths tildify** to `~/projects/vscode`. ### Notes for reviewers - The hover widget is shared with the editor window's `agent-host-session://` chat pills, so both adapters were updated. The Agents window now formats paths through `ILabelService.getUriLabel`, which replaces a hand-rolled `uri.scheme === file ? fsPath : toString()` helper — that also fixes remote and virtual workspaces, which previously showed a raw URI string. The editor window only ever has opaque path strings (not URIs) and so calls the `tildify` primitive directly; that rewrites only a path genuinely under the local home, leaving a remote session's path alone. - `tildify` is a deliberate no-op on Windows, matching how the rest of VS Code renders paths. The shortening is macOS/Linux only. - `getSessionSummaryHoverData` gained `IOpenerService` and `ILabelService` parameters, which is most of the churn in `sessionsList.ts`. - Component fixture baselines will need refreshing — the hover's appearance changed. ### Validation `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check` and hygiene pass; the affected unit tests pass. 1. Open a file somewhere where saving it is really slow (e.g. an NFS mount).
2. Edit it.
3. Press Ctrl-S, Ctrl-W really quickly.

What can sometimes happen is that it shows the "Do you want to save the changes you made to <file>? [Save] [Don't Save] [Cancel]" dialog, even though you already pressed Ctrl-S.

Presumably the close-file handler checks if the file has unsaved changes and if so it shows that dialog.

It's very annoying for things like editing Git commit messages.

title: fix: clear terminal drag-and-drop observer on detach (fixes #311164)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #311164.
Supersedes #318756 with requested unit tests and race condition guards.

`TerminalInstance._dndObserver` (a `MutableDisposable<IDisposable>` holding the per-container `DragAndDropObserver`) was set by `_initDragAndDrop` but never cleared by `detachFromElement`. When a `TerminalEditor` pane reuses its container across tab switches (`setInput` calls `detachFromElement` on the old instance and `attachToElement` on the new one), newly-attached terminals stacked additional `DragAndDropObserver`s on top of leaked ones.

When shift-dropping a file onto the active editor-area terminal, each previous instance's observer fired on the shared container and inserted the path.

### Changes
1. Dispose `this._dndObserver.clear()` in `detachFromElement()` so drops on the old container no longer route to the detached terminal instance.
2. Guard the deferred `setTimeout` in `attachToElement` with `if (this._store.isDisposed || this._container !== container) return;` so a synchronous detach in the same tick does not re-attach a stale observer.
3. Added unit tests in `terminalInstance.test.ts` verifying that `detachFromElement` properly clears the observer.

Co-authored-by: Vlad Gerasimov <vlad@vlad.studio>

title: run_in_terminal reports premature completion and Ctrl+C's the running command (Windows, PowerShell 7/ConPTY)
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.63.2026082502
- VS Code Version: 1.135.0-insider
- OS Version: Windows 11 (10.0.26200.0), x64
- Feature: agent
- Selected model: Claude Opus 4.8

## Steps to Reproduce:

1. In Copilot agent mode on Windows with the PowerShell integrated terminal, have the agent run a **long-running** command as a normal (sync) `run_in_terminal` call — e.g. a multi-minute build that redirects output to a file:
   `.\build.cmd -subset clr.corelib -c Debug > out.log 2>&1`
2. Issue several such calls **back-to-back** across the session (build → read status → build again). Incremental/fast-starting builds trigger it most reliably.
3. Intermittently, the tool returns after **~100–500 ms** with the terminal showing `PS D:\...> ^C` (or, for a build, the redirected log ends mid-run with `Attempting to cancel the build...`). The command was **not** finished — the tool sent `Ctrl+C` (SIGINT) to the terminal and reported the call as complete.

---

## Summary

VS Code's `run_in_terminal` chat tool intermittently sends **`Ctrl+C` (SIGINT)** to the persistent PowerShell terminal and **cancels a command that is still running**. It appears the tool mistakes a shell‑integration command‑boundary desync for command completion: it returns almost immediately and, in reclaiming the terminal, interrupts the live process. This happens on **Windows + PowerShell 7 (ConPTY)** with **no custom prompt** — i.e. distinct from the zsh/powerlevel10k reports, though likely the same underlying "SIGINT from PromptInputModel incorrectly used in chat terminal tool result" defect.

Impact: long builds/tests are silently killed a few hundred ms after starting; the agent sees a phantom cancellation, retries, and burns cycles. Only `mode=async` + file‑redirect + polling reliably avoids it.

## Evidence (sanitized, from Copilot Chat debug logs)

Source: `<USER>\AppData\Roaming\Code - Insiders\User\workspaceStorage\<WS>\GitHub.copilot-chat\debug-logs\<SESSION>\main.jsonl`. Each row is one `run_in_terminal` `tool_call`; `dur` is how long the tool waited before returning; every one has `status:"ok"` and the **next** logged event is a normal `llm_request` (i.e. *no* user message interrupted — the cancel was tool‑initiated, not user‑initiated).

| # | Command (sync) | `dur` | `timeout` | Result / effect |
|---|----------------|-------|-----------|-----------------|
| A | `git add …; git commit -m "…"` | **128 ms** | — | Result was literally `PS D:\...> ^C`. A commit cannot finish in 128 ms. |
| B | `.\build.cmd -subset clr.corelib … > corelib-win2.log` | **187 ms** | 600000 | The redirected log **ends mid‑restore** with `Attempting to cancel the build...` — SIGINT reached MSBuild 187 ms in, ~3000× below the 10‑min timeout. |
| C | `.\build.cmd -subset clr.corelib … > corelib-win3.log` | **297 ms** | 600000 | Result `PS D:\...> ^C`; its log shows 3 task DLLs built, then `Attempting to cancel the build...`. |
| D | `Start-Sleep -Seconds 1; …` | **95 ms** | — | Result `PS D:\...> ^C` — a 1‑second sleep was interrupted at 95 ms. |

Contrast — the same kind of sync build **succeeds** when the desync does not occur:

| # | Command (sync) | `dur` | Result |
|---|----------------|-------|--------|
| E | `.\build.cmd -subset clr.corelib …` (first, full build) | **83,975 ms** | Completed, exit 0 |
| F | `.\dotnet.cmd build …\System.Net.Sockets.csproj` | **135,221 ms** | Completed, exit 0 |
| G | same corelib build launched with **`mode=async`** | ran to completion | Completed, exit 0 |

Representative captured output for case B (a *file read* issued right after, showing the build's own truncated log):

```
  Determining projects to restore...
  ...
  Restore was successful.
  All projects are up-to-date for restore.
  Determining projects to restore...
  All projects are up-to-date for restore.
Attempting to cancel the build...      <-- log ends here; MSBuild received SIGINT
```

A recurring cosmetic signal in the async terminal snapshots was PSReadLine **re‑rendering the long command line ~10×** (the same `PS D:\...> .\build.cmd …` echoed repeatedly), which corrupts the OSC‑633 command‑boundary markers.

## Analysis / root cause

- The cancel is **tool‑initiated**, not the user and not a real 130: for every affected call the following event is a normal model round‑trip, and unaffected long builds (E/F/G) prove the command itself is fine.
- `dur` of 95–297 ms with a `600000 ms` timeout rules out a timeout.
- The redirected build logs literally end with MSBuild's `Attempting to cancel the build...`, proving a **SIGINT was delivered to the running process**, not just a misread exit code.
- It correlates with back‑to‑back invocations and PSReadLine re‑rendering of long command lines → the shell‑integration command **start/end (OSC 633 C/D)** markers desync; the tool reads a stale "command finished" from the *previous* command, returns, and sends `Ctrl+C` to reclaim the terminal — hitting the still‑running new command.
- This is the Windows/PowerShell/ConPTY manifestation of the same class as microsoft/vscode#271902 ("SIGINT from PromptInputModel being incorrectly used in chat terminal tool result"), but reproduces **without** powerlevel10k/zsh, so the ConPTY + PSReadLine path needs its own look.

## Related issues (search performed)

- microsoft/vscode#271902 — *Investigate SIGINT from PromptInputModel being incorrectly used in chat terminal tool result* (Open, `chat-terminal`, `terminal-shell-zsh`). Closest match; currently framed around zsh/p10k forwarding a 130. This report adds a **Windows + pwsh, no‑custom‑prompt** repro.
- microsoft/vscode#259677 / #271897 — *premature command completion (~10s)* (Closed/dup). Same premature‑completion family; partially addressed by #261431 (re‑evaluate shell integration each use) + logging #262903.
- microsoft/vscode#291871 — *agent thinks command exited 130 while it exited 0*.
- microsoft/vscode#278967 — *Copilot always gets stuck when performing second terminal command*.

If maintainers consider this the same defect as #271902, please treat this as a Windows/pwsh data point rather than a new issue.

## Workaround (verified)

Run long commands with **`mode=async`**, redirect output to a log, and write an exit sentinel; then poll the sentinel — do not run them as sync foreground commands, and never chain `Start-Sleep`:

```powershell
.\build.cmd <args> *> build.log; "exit=$LASTEXITCODE" | Out-File build.status
# then, separately: Get-Content build.status ; Get-Content build.log -Tail 20
```

## Fix proposal

1. **Do not send `Ctrl+C` to reclaim the terminal on tool return unless the command's OSC‑633 `D` (command‑finished) marker was actually observed.** If completion is uncertain, background/detach the command instead of interrupting it.
2. **Distinguish tool‑initiated cancellation from a genuine `130`/SIGINT** originating in the program (the crux of #271902), including a ConPTY/PowerShell code path — the desync here occurs with a plain PSReadLine prompt, so it is not specific to p10k.
3. **Harden command‑boundary detection against PSReadLine re‑rendering** of long command lines (repeated prompt redraws) that interleave/duplicate OSC markers; e.g. correlate the `C`/`D` nonce per command rather than by position.
4. Add a diagnostic (extending the logging from #262903) that records *why* the tool returned (observed `D` marker vs. fallback timer vs. reclaim‑SIGINT) so these cases are attributable from the Terminal output channel.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue was drafted with GitHub Copilot.

Type: Feature Request Currently, when you place a cursor over a "symbol" in your code, it shows a detail hover panel that carries information about that symbol. You can move your cursor into that hover panel, and when your cursor moves outside it, it disappears. This poses a very discomforting user experience challenge when you try to copy part of the content in that hover panel (e.g. the type definition of a function) because when you hold down your cursor and start dragging to highlight the part you want to copy, your cursor often moves outside the hover panel (as dragging in straight line is difficult to do) and it keeps disappearing as a result. I'm proposing a pinning mechanism that keeps the panel in focus and locked in, even when your cursor goes outside it. Maybe something like holding down CTRL and hovering over a symbol keeps the hover panel pinned and you can move in with your cursor to highlight and copy stuff. title: agentHost: clarify artifact file URI schema
body:
## Summary

- clarify that `add_artifact_or_reference` file and resource values must be absolute URIs
- include valid and invalid Windows path examples in the model-facing schema
- cover the advertised schema contract with a unit test

## Why

Recent Agent Host logs showed a model passing a plain Windows file-system path and hitting the stricter runtime validator:

```
Invalid add_artifact_or_reference input: uri must be an absolute URI including its scheme, such as 'file:///path/to/file' — not a plain file system path.
```

The validator was correct, but the tool schema only described the field as a URI. Advertising the actual absolute-URI requirement and a concrete Windows `file:` URI prevents invalid tool calls at the producer.

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/artifactServerTools.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/artifactServerTools.test.ts`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\artifactServerTools.test.ts` (5 passing)
- `git diff --check`

`npm run hygiene` could not start on Windows because its existing `import.meta.url` path handling resolved `remote/package.json` as `C:\C:\Code\...\remote\package.json`.

title: agentHost: Avoid error log for successful Copilot shutdown
body:
The Copilot SDK writes its successful shutdown-completion diagnostic to stderr. The Agent Host launcher currently classifies all non-allowlisted stderr as errors, resulting in misleading `[error]` entries during normal shutdown.

Add the SDK shutdown-completion message to the existing expected-stderr allowlist. Actual SDK failures continue to be logged as errors.

title: Fix Git-root detection for submodules in Copilot extension
body:
Fixes #329169

This pull request addresses issue #329169 by refining the Git-root detection logic in the Copilot extension. The changes ensure that only a **`.git` directory** is treated as the repository root, allowing traversal past a submodule’s **`.git` file** to the enclosing superproject.

### Changes Made
- Updated the parent-repository discovery logic in:
  - `promptFilesLocator.ts`
  - `agentInstructionsLocator.ts`
- Added regression tests to validate the new behavior in:
  - `promptFilesLocator.test.ts`
  - `agentInstructionsLocator.spec.ts`

### Validation Results
- All core focused tests (6) and Copilot extension locator tests (14) passed.
- Type checks and diff checks were successful, confirming the integrity of the changes. 

This fix enhances the functionality of the Copilot extension by correctly handling submodule scenarios, ensuring a more robust user experience.
